newsitem.title: ITALY: Middle East to have own Disney Channel in April.
newsitem.headline: Middle East to have own Disney Channel in April.

text.p: ORBIT, a Saudi-owned satellite relay station based in Rome, said on Friday that it would launch a specially tailored Disney Channel to the Middle East and Africa on April 2, 1997.

"The Disney Channel will be specifically tailored to the region's tastes and interests, featuring world famous Disney productions complimented by additional required programming," Orbit said in a statement.
It said the channel, created exclusively for Orbit by Disney, would provide "quality family programming to viewers in 23 countries across the Middle East and North Africa."
It said that, as with all of Orbit's channels, Disney would be available on an a-la-carte basis to network subscribers.
An Orbit spokeswoman said The Disney Channel would provide a 24-hour service either in Arabic or with subtitles.
The spokeswoman said all Disney Channels were tailored for their specific markets. Industry sources said the programming would respect cultural and religious sensitivities.
Orbit is a 24-hour fully digital, multi-channel pay-television service. It broadcasts more than 30 channels to 23 countries.
Orbit said it would also be adding nine STAR TV channels in 1997 in addition to The Disney Channel.
